draft.title: Profitability ratios
card: A profitability ratio compares a profit figure with something else, as a percentage. Each ratio shows profit from a different angle.
Gross profit margin
gross profit ÷ sales × 100. It shows how much of each sales dollar is left after the cost of the goods sold.
Net profit margin
net profit ÷ sales × 100. It shows how much of each sales dollar is left after all expenses.
Return on assets
net profit ÷ average total assets × 100. It shows the profit earned from each dollar of assets the business uses.
Return on owner's investment
net profit ÷ average owner's equity × 100. It shows the profit earned on the money the owner has put in.
draft.remember: Each profitability ratio is profit divided by something: sales, assets or the owner's equity.

a.q: Which ratio shows the profit earned on each dollar of the owner's equity?
a.why: Return on owner's investment divides net profit by average owner's equity. Return on assets looks tempting, but it divides by total assets, which include assets funded by more than the owner's equity.
a.clue: Look at what each ratio divides the profit by.

b.q: Ravi's bike shop in Ballarat had sales of $200,000, gross profit of $80,000 and net profit of $20,000. What is its net profit margin?
b.why: Net profit margin = net profit ÷ sales × 100 = 20,000 ÷ 200,000 × 100 = 10%. The 40% result is the gross profit margin, which uses gross profit instead of net profit.
b.clue: Use net profit, not gross profit, and divide by sales.

problems.detail: The stem asks about 'the owner's equity', and 'Return on owner's investment' is the only option containing the word 'owner's'. A student can match the words and pick it without knowing what each ratio divides by.

check.summary: The formulas and answers are correct: return on owner's investment for (a) and 10% for (b). In question a, the word 'owner's' in the stem matches only the right option, so students can guess it from the wording.

proposal.title: Profitability ratios
card: Gross profit margin
gross profit ÷ sales × 100. It shows how much of each sales dollar is left after the cost of the goods sold.
Net profit margin
net profit ÷ sales × 100. It shows how much of each sales dollar is left after all expenses.
Return on assets
net profit ÷ average total assets × 100. It shows the profit earned from each dollar of assets the business uses, however they were funded.
Return on owner's investment
net profit ÷ average owner's equity × 100. Owner's equity is the capital the owner has in the business, so this shows the return on the owner's own money.
proposal.remember: Each profitability ratio is profit divided by something: sales, assets or the owner's equity.

a.q: Jo wants to know if the capital she has in her business earns more than a term deposit would. Which ratio should she use?
a.why: Jo's capital is her owner's equity, and return on owner's investment divides net profit by average owner's equity. Return on assets is tempting, but it divides by total assets, which include assets funded by liabilities as well as by Jo.
a.clue: Which ratio divides profit by the money Jo herself has put in?

b.q: Ravi's bike shop in Ballarat had sales of $200,000, gross profit of $80,000 and net profit of $20,000. What is its net profit margin?
b.why: Net profit margin = net profit ÷ sales × 100 = 20,000 ÷ 200,000 × 100 = 10%. The 40% result is the gross profit margin, which uses gross profit instead of net profit.
b.clue: Use net profit, not gross profit, and divide by sales.
